Title: Disappointing Experience at Pure Gym Chelmsford

I recently visited Pure Gym Chelmsford with high hopes of a fulfilling workout session, but unfortunately, my experience fell short of expectations. My visit was marred by a multitude of issues, primarily revolving around faulty equipment and a disappointing lack of adherence to basic gym etiquette.

Firstly, the state of the equipment was appalling. Several machines were out of order, with no indication of when they would be fixed. This not only limited the variety of exercises I could perform but also resulted in unnecessary waiting times as other patrons jostled for the few functioning machines available. It's disheartening to pay for a gym membership only to find oneself unable to use essential equipment due to maintenance neglect.

Furthermore, the overall gym atmosphere left much to be desired in terms of cleanliness and organization. The gym floor seemed perpetually cluttered, making it difficult to navigate between machines without bumping into other gym-goers or abandoned equipment. The lack of regular cleaning was evident, with sweat-stained benches and sticky floors detracting from the overall experience.

But perhaps most disappointing was the lack of respect for gym etiquette among fellow patrons. There was a notable absence of individuals re-racking weights or wiping down machines after use, creating an unhygienic and chaotic environment. It's disconcerting to witness such blatant disregard for basic gym rules, which ultimately detracts from the experience for everyone present.

Overall, my visit to Pure Gym Chelmsford was a regrettable one. The combination of faulty equipment, poor cleanliness, and a lack of adherence to gym etiquette significantly diminished the quality of my workout. For those seeking a reliable and well-maintained gym environment, I would advise looking elsewhere until these issues are addressed and resolved.

There is a huge range of free weights everywhere as well, more than one section also.
-The gym has clear and considerate rules that most if not all follow exactly, and it makes it clear that if rules are not followed you get removed, which puts me at ease as I feel less endangered.
-The gym’s locker/shower/toilet rooms are separated by sex- but what makes it safe is that there’s a unique element where after a certain time (in the night) you need pin access to enter so there’s no way for the opposite sex to enter the wrong room and make anyone feel uncomfortable.
-You don’t see staff as soon as you walk in. This might seem like a bad thing to some individuals but for many people (including myself) it’s quite intimidating to see a staff member as soon as you walk in who’s usually already in amazing shape to greet you via social interaction. It’s nice that we can access the gym ourselves with the PIN code/ bar code and it means that I don’t immediately feel stress and insecurity as soon as I walk into the gym.
-There are motivational messages all over the place! Even when I get a drink from the flavoured water machine it usually says something like “Are those new muscles we see?” Or “Keep up the good work” etc. The walls are plastered with messages about how progress matters and things like that. It personally helps me keep my energy up and keep working out even when I start to give up.

Overall I feel like these perks make the gym unique and it truly makes it enjoyable to work out, even for someone like me who struggles with obesity and only started off a few months ago!! The gym etiquette is also very lovely, everyone is very friendly and minds their own business, I feel like the gym is partially responsible for the comfortable community-like vibe for the same reasons I would recommend this gym to everyone.

Its a decent little gym, good for beginners, but not all that great for those who are more familiar with the gym.
Equipment is newbie friendly and there are means of usage that allow the experienced lifters to get a good workout.
Biggest gripes (more than one issue) I can come up with is that the free weight area is tiny and as a result, not a lot of benches, and those usually get jacked to be used at the squating racks or smith machines, which means that at any given time roughly 4 to 5 of those benches may be dragged out.
That being said, yeah, not a lot of squat racks, and only 2 smith machines, which in itself is not that bad, but this is a commerical gym, so expect these to be in use most of the time you are there.
To add to the fact that this gym is newbie friendly, there are going to be people in there who have never been in a gym, good for them for taking that step. However, I do believe that some form of introduction as a standard for every new member should be a thing, there are times I am afraid to begin my workout due to somebody running around not paying attention. Again, nothing against people that take that first step, just it can be a bit of a scare when somebody unfamiliar with the gym does not give ample space avoiding potential injury to you or them, an intro should be something people should opt into, though I understand such a thing would be hard to set up consistantly.
The additonal racks in the centre can be used for squats, but I do recommend bumper plates as there is no means of preventing the bar from hitting the ground if you are to fail a rep.
Quite a bit of cardio machines, not excessive, which is a bit surprising for a commercial gym, but don't expect 50 treadmills to 1 squat rack.
Oh, and do bring earphones or headphones, sometimes if you just so happen to be in the area a lesson is happening, the music will cause your eardrums to burst, seriously, it is that loud and it made for some uncomfortable workouts, even with earbuds in.
Other than that, it is a bog standard commercial gym, it is not good for any serious powerlifting, trust me that there are better optins for powerlifitng than puregym. But other than that, its open 24/7, its convenient and a membership isn't going to empty your pockets thouroughly each month. For bodybuilding and general cardio, this is the gym you should be considering as an option. Not bad, not great, just so so, do recommend this to most first time gym goers.

I've been a loyal member of Pure Gym Urban Exchange for over 5 years now, so I've seen its evolution firsthand. There's a lot to appreciate here, starting with its local presence and the quality of the equipment available. The gym has everything you need for a comprehensive workout, from cardio machines to free weights.

However, its popularity, although a testament to its value, does bring about some challenges. During peak hours, the gym can feel a bit overcrowded, which is further compounded by the fact that equipment is often left out instead of being put back in its place. This not only creates a chaotic environment but also makes it difficult to find and use equipment efficiently.

A significant portion of the gym floor is frequently 'reserved' for classes during these peak times. This means that even as the gym buzzes with members, access to essential equipment is restricted, which can be frustrating for those of us looking to get in a full workout.

One of the most pressing issues, however, is the gym's ventilation. The air conditioning system seems to be perpetually out of order, or perhaps it's not being utilized as it should be. This has led to excessive condensation on the walls and windows, making the gym uncomfortably humid and warm. It's not just a matter of discomfort; it feels like a health and safety oversight.

Cleanliness is another area where Pure Gym Urban Exchange could significantly improve. Despite the presence of cleaners, their efforts seem superficial, with dust accumulation clearly visible across the gym. A more thorough cleaning regime would greatly enhance the workout environment.

Pure Gym Urban Exchange has all the makings of a flagship facility for the brand. Its popularity among locals is a clear indicator of its potential. However, this same popularity is contributing to its drawbacks, particularly in terms of cleanliness and equipment management. There's a real opportunity here for Pure Gym to address these issues head-on and elevate the gym to a standard that not only meets but exceeds members' expectations. After more than half a decade of membership, I hope to see these changes implemented, for the betterment of all gym-goers.

Embarking on a fitness journey at my local gym has been an adventure akin to navigating the darker recesses of a post-apocalyptic wasteland, where the only semblance of civilization is the communal struggle for survival... or in this case, hygiene and hydration.

Firstly, the urinal situation is a fascinating study in modern art - a single, perpetually broken monument that serves more as a mausoleum for abandoned chewing gum than a functional piece of plumbing. The aromatic bouquet of urine that wafts through the toilets and changing rooms adds a certain je ne sais quoi, creating an ambiance that screams, "Abandon all hope, ye who enter here." The soap dispenser, singular in its loneliness, stands by the sink, a testament to missed opportunities and squandered potential, whispering tales of what could have been in a world where two dispensers could have flourished.

Venturing further into the heart of darkness, the water fountain saga is a thrilling tale of endurance and patience. At peak times, a congregation of parched souls forms a line reminiscent of the bread queues in Soviet Russia, each member awaiting their turn to partake in the trickle of life itself. The solution seems simple: out with the old, in with a new fountain capable of spewing water with the ferocity of a fire hose, lest we all perish from dehydration or die of old age in the queue.

Lastly, the gym members, a delightful bunch, seem to have taken a collective vow against the tyranny of literacy and order. The weights, in a defiant protest against gravity and common sense, are scattered in a chaotic symphony of iron and rubber. This disregard for organizational norms could be seen as a bold statement against the oppressive regime of labels and designated spots, or perhaps it's just a testament to the educational system's failure to instill the value of "putting things back where they belong."

In conclusion, navigating this gym is not for the faint of heart. It requires a resilience and sense of humor as robust as the gum-clogged urinal.

As a 66-year-old woman living with diabetes and experiencing significant muscle loss, I was initially hesitant about starting a physical fitness journey. The thought of joining a gym was daunting, especially at my age and with my health concerns. Nevertheless, I joined PureGym Hammersmith, and I'm really glad I did.
PureGym Hammersmith Palais has wide array of machines, facilities and spacious workout areas. What truly sets this gym apart, though, is its incredibly attentive and responsive staff. As someone new to the gym scene, I was surprised by the welcoming and friendly atmosphere. It felt like stepping into a supportive community, not just a workout space.
Most of all, Melanie, my personal trainer, is what has made this an amazing experience. Melanie has been a blessing on my fitness journey. Her professional support, with her empathetic encouragement, have really helped me. Melanie's approach is not just about physical training; it's about building confidence, discipline, and resilience. After 53 training sessions together, the results speak for themselves. I've gained 2 kilos of muscle mass, seen a general increase in strength, and improved my mobility. Even more encouraging are the gradual improvements in my blood glucose levels, and overall, I feel fantastic mentally.
To anyone considering a gym, especially those who might feel intimidated by age or health conditions, PureGym Hammersmith Palais is a wonderful choice. And if you can, hire a personal trainer like Melanie. Her invaluable support has transformed this challenge into one of the most rewarding experiences of my life. Thank you, Mel, for everything.

Spacious Layout: The gym feels airy and uncrowded, even during peak hours, providing ample space to move around and train comfortably.
Group Classes: A diverse range of classes, from spinning and HIIT to yoga and pilates, adds variety and motivation to my routine.
Affordable Membership: Compared to other gyms in the area, PureGym offers competitive monthly fees, making it a budget-friendly option.

Temperature Control:

The gym can get uncomfortably cold during winter months, particularly in the free weights area. Improved heating is needed for optimal comfort.
Maintenance Issues: Some equipment, especially in the cardio zone, shows signs of wear and tear, requiring prompt repair or replacement.
Crowded Showers: During peak hours, the shower facilities can become congested, causing waiting times and inconvenience. Expanding the shower stall availability would be beneficial.
Limited Parking: The parking lot can fill up quickly, especially during evenings and weekends. Consider exploring additional parking options or implementing clear signage to guide members to available spaces.
Clientele Mix: While most members are respectful, a small minority engage in disruptive behavior such as dropping weights and disregarding gym etiquette. More active staff presence and reminders of gym etiquette could create a more positive training environment for everyone.

Cons:

Shower/toilet rooms

I am not a fan of this gym. I thought of the potential when I noticed a new gym near my home and thought I would join and check it out. It seemed interesting, clean, had decent equipment, and an abundance of cardio machines (I needed to lose weight). However, the first thing that annoyed me was one of the employees approached me to say I am not allowed to have a gym bag on the floor (which was between two ellipticals), but I acquiesced.

The next thing that bothered me was an email I received late at night that my account was locked because my payment did not go through. Admittedly, this was my fault because I keep my card locked to avoid scammers stealing money from my account (it has happened many times in NoVA). I unlocked my card and went to pay to unlock my account and noticed there was a $15 “admin fee.” I paid it and didn’t think too much of it. However, considering I paid the fee and my account was unlocked immediately at 1 am, I wondered what was the purpose of an admin fee if the computer does the work.

Moving forward, I didn’t complain and kept going and paying my payments. Then, two months later, I run into the same problem (admittedly my fault because I forgot to unlock my card). So, I write to customer service asking about the admin fee and why they didn’t try the payment a second time. The rep told me that they are not required to do so and the contract states that there is a section of the contract that says an admin fee is attached when payments do not go through. Ok, fair. However, I then ask where in the contract does it say the admin fee is $15. She gives me the section in the contract and I scour the entire document to find no mention of it.

When I responded to her email and told here there was no mention of a $15 admin fee, she had a guy respond to tell me that he removed the fee and pasted something from the contract that I didn’t read at the time because the fee was gone. The next month, same think happened (again, locked card-my fault). So, I made the change and found the email response from the gentleman who pasted a passage that says “Membership Dues.’  ‘Membership Dues’ consist of all dues applicable to the membership including, without limitation, any Daily, Monthly, of Fixed Term membership fees, the Annual Maintenance Fee, and other administrative fees permitted by this Agreement.”

He then says that fees can increase of decrease, which is why the $15 isn’t mentioned. Ok, for those who read this review, particularly Pure Fitness management, let me give you a little lesson on contract law. In the state of Virginia, there is this legal principle called “Contra proferentum,” which means that interpreting a contract that includes ambiguous, or unclear terms, the interpretation must benefit of the one who did not draft the agreement. Therefore, without the explicit definition of what constitutes an “admin fee,” they legally cannot apply this charge to any member. Reason being, the absence of a defined cost, if deemed legal, would give them the power to charge a member an admin fee of $50, $100, $200. The fact that they only attempt the charge once and immediately apply the admin fee just reeks of unethical business practices.

Whilst doing this, they also stray too close to others who are working out (leaving me focusing less on my technique and more on not dropping a weight on one of them), and weights / equipment are left all over the place.

Likewise, far too many times I’ve watched someone waiting patiently for equipment (which is apparently in use as possessions are on them) only for an individual to come over from the other side of the room and pick those possessions up 10 minutes later once they’re done chatting with friends. This has happened to me so many times and when challenged, I’ve received a shrug.

Frustratingly, this poor behaviour consistently goes completely unchallenged by staff when present. As said, I’ve challenged this behaviour personally but it shouldn’t come to that.

I completely understand that a gym isn’t a library and it is a core place for young people to exercise / socialise (as I have done since I was a teenager), but there are levels of acceptable behaviour and such behaviour shouldn’t infringe on the experience of others.

As a result of this behaviour - which has been consistent during my time but has noticeably increased over the past 5 months - and the general level of busyness, I’ve moved to a different gym in the area. PureGym is a great place and great value for the area, but there needs to be a concerted effort by staff to show that such behaviour highlighted is not acceptable.

Title: PureGym Palmers Green: A Convenient Fitness Hub with Room for Improvement

PureGym Palmers Green has established itself as a convenient and affordable fitness haven, offering a comprehensive range of equipment and a welcoming atmosphere. While the gym's squat machine is particularly impressive, some areas, such as the toilets and cleaning services, could benefit from enhanced attention.

The gym's extensive array of machines caters to diverse fitness goals, ensuring that members can find the equipment they need to achieve their workout objectives. The squat machine, in particular, stands out as an exceptional addition, providing ample support and stability for effective squat training.

The gym's convenient location and flexible opening hours make it a valuable asset for busy individuals seeking to fit fitness into their hectic schedules. The 24/7 access allows members to structure their workouts around their busy lives, providing flexibility and convenience.

However, some areas of the gym could benefit from improvement. The recurring issue of out-of-order toilets can be inconvenient and detract from the overall gym experience. Additionally, the lack of adequate staff presence can lead to longer waiting times at reception and a less personalized service.

Furthermore, the cleanliness of the gym could be enhanced. While the general cleanliness is acceptable, there have been instances of equipment being left unclean or not properly sanitized. A more consistent and thorough cleaning routine would elevate the overall cleanliness and hygiene of the gym.

Overall, PureGym Palmers Green offers a solid foundation for fitness enthusiasts, providing a convenient and affordable space to pursue their workout goals. The extensive range of equipment, particularly the squat machine, is a significant draw. However, addressing the issues with out-of-order facilities, limited staff presence, and inconsistent cleaning would further enhance the gym's overall appeal and satisfaction among its members.

Pros:

- Fair range and quantity of equipment.

- Affordable price point. At £21 per month it is cheaper than most options in the area.

- Decent number of classes with friendly trainers. Those who are already fit, like circuits, and like being pushed to their limit will like it here.

- Location at the retail park makes popping to the shops after a workout easy.

Cons:

- Always dirty and messy. There is nothing to wipe equipment down with, many do not put their weights away, and no staff monitor or remedy this meaning plates are left on equipment, the floor, and anywhere but they should be.
When we've mentioned this to staff we're told this doesn't happen, but we have plenty of picture proof that says otherwise.

- The classes aren't varied, aren't beginner friendly, and one of the LBT classes is run by a bully. I used to enjoy LBT at my last gym but Antoni put me off doing another class here ever again. At multiple points we were told if we stopped or tried to take a break, he would make everyone else do more reps. For example, he told us to do a 2 minute plank, which is not common practice, and "if anyone's knees touched the floor" he would "restart the timer". The lady next to me was struggling to complete the reps at another point so he decided to belittle her in front of everyone and add more weights to her bar without permission. I think if Antoni wanted to act like a drill sergeant he should have tried his luck at a boot camp rather than bullying a class of women. The approach might work for some, but it's highly inappropriate for a chain gym.

- You have to pay for yoga and zumba which makes the "low cost" part of Puregym redundant if you want to do those classes. Like many, I am someone who does not like sitting on a treadmill or cross trainer on the days I need to put down the weights and do cardio, and I love yoga to round out my cardio and weight training. Unfortunately, many of the classes revolve around circuits or cycling, which I don't like. The dance classes are too infrequent, and you must pay an added fee for them. By the time you pay an additional £2-£4 per week you may as well go to Bannatynes or the Village gyms where you get a pool, spa, and access to a lot more classes including different types of yoga, dance fitness and Thai Chi for no additional charge. To put it into perspective, I pay £27 per month for my plus membership and if I did two yoga/dance classes per week it would bump that up to £43. At that point why not pay £50 p/m for a higher-end gym with a pool and better services? Well, I'm going to 🤷🏻‍♀️

- The retail park location means you often have to queue in traffic to get in and out, especially on weekends. I don't go during rush hour in the week or on Saturdays if I can help it. It also means this puregym isn't 24 hours as I believe the car park has to be closed overnight.

- During mornings (6 - 8am), and I imagine at peak times, it's hard to get on some equipment. There aren't enough smith machines, squat racks, or leg presses. There is one incline leg press machine in the building. It can also be hard to find a  cable machine, despite there being many in the gym, as they're either busy or not the correct one (they have two different types and the weights vary between them making consistency hard if you're forced to use the other if you're used to one). This means you often have to wait for equipment which isn't always viable if you have to get to work.

We came to Bristol for a weekend break and I usually come to the area maybe three or four times a year and always felt guilty about neglecting exercising because i didn't know there was a PureGym in the area.

PureGym Bristol Central was a mere three-minute walk from my hotel at Travelodge Central and i liked that i didn't even need to bring much because it was that close to the hotel.

We first came here this weekend and we did get a bit lost walking around the building but i think it was the Google Maps placement that made it look like it was opposite Pizza Express but it isn't.

We came into the building and it was a standard capsule entry where you have to enter your pin to get access to the gym.  You then need to take the lift up to either the 4th floor (the main section) or the 5th floor where the lockers and changing room are.

I initially thought it was a bit of a confusing layout because it was a different style of building compared to the other gyms i have been to under the same PureGym franchise.

We liked that the lockers here are bigger than the standard sizes so we could fit in a backpack instead of just being given space for a phone and maybe some change. The changing rooms here were bigger and i liked the showers, I didn't have a chance to use them because my hotel was literally around the corner but they looked high quality. The glass door was a little off-putting but it hid the private areas so i guess that's something.

We used the treadmill first, this was an older style of treadmill than my local and it even had the connection points for an iPod. However, they were all on standby mode meaning it looked kike it wasn't working but you have to press the green "Go" for up to eight seconds before it reboots.

I liked that there were multiple of the same machine meaning i could choose where i wanted to run but some of them were unusable due to some of them facing the bright white building that the sun was reflecting and i wonder if that was more suited for the clouder days perhaps.

I had a good run and then i tried some of the weights, this is not down to the company but the customers themselves who would leave huge sports bags and jackets on some of the machines when they were not using them. This seemed to be accepted by the community and it really shouldn't be.

Otherwise, it was a great gym and i am glad i visited, it is nice that i could exercise while being away from home and i like how it is open 24 7 meaning i can choose when i can exercise.

I would rate this gym 3.5 stars and most of those stars come from the classes, which unfortunately are ever decreasing since I joined. I think most (not all) of the trainers at this gym are fantastic and run really good classes that can be easy/basic if you want but that also allow you to challenge yourself if you choose to by adding heavier weights or doing more difficult variations. There is a tendency towards cardio in the Les Mills-style of high reps of lower weights but I find that signing up for classes which are included in the membership fee keeps me accountable and ensures I get a workout in. That said, the classes do tend to be very popular with the best ones being hard to get into and it should be noted that having a booking doesn’t always guaranty you a spot in the class as all the good ones tend to be really full with (I suspect) people who didn’t sign up or who were waitlisted coming as well.

Which brings me to the part of this gym that drags the reviews down- the fact that you can’t come in knowing what your workout will be. It all depends on what’s available. The gym is consistently crowded unless you come in the middle of the afternoon before or after the lunchtime rush OR are there like on a weekend evening. Otherwise forget accessing a squat rack or any kind of bench or any resistance machines.  And if you do, someone is probably waiting behind you, so you feel a bit rushed. That said, if you can figure out a workout that uses dumbbells and kettlebells, you can usually find a corner to work out.

Cleanliness-wise, it’s fine. The current renovation has made things more chaotic and crowded than they used to be and strangely despite this fact, one of the things there seems to be less of are the self-cleaning stations which is a bit gross.

I know I could do a lot better in terms of gym, but I think for the price, the value is REALLY good and it serves its purpose.

Zunächst möchte ich betonen, dass ich grundsätzlich zufrieden bin mit Ihrem Fitnessangebot in Rorschach und die Einrichtungen gerne und oft nutze. Dennoch gibt es dringende Anliegen, welche meine Erfahrungen in Ihrem Fitnessstudio erheblich beeinträchtigen.

In den letzten Monaten habe ich wiederholt feststellen müssen, dass viele Geräte und Maschinen in Ihrem Studio defekt sind.
Besonders besorgniserregend ist für mich, dass aktuell die Adduktoren Maschine seit mindestens 6 Wochen ausser Betrieb zu sein scheint. Ich verstehe einfach nicht, wie es dazu kommen kann, dass ein so grundlegendes Gerät für eine derart lange
Zeitspanne nicht repariert wurde.

Was mich besonders frustriert, ist der Vergleich mit anderen Fitnesscenter, bei denen ich Mitglied war. In diesen Einrichtungen wurden defekte Geräte in der Regel innerhalb von einer Woche repariert. Die Tatsache, dass in Ihrem Fitnessstudio derartige Verzögerungen bei Reparaturen auftreten, ist für mich nicht nachvollziehbar.

Als zahlendes Mitglied erwarte ich, dass die Geräte in Ihrem Fitnessstudio in gutem Zustand sind. Die anhaltenden Probleme mit defekten Maschinen beeinträchtigen nicht nur meine Trainingsroutine, sondern auch die der restlichen Mitglieder und schlussendlich ebenso meine Gesamtzufriedenheit als Mitglied.
Ich bitte daher dringend darum, dass Sie diese Angelegenheit ernsthaft in Angriff nehmen und Massnahmen ergreifen, um sicherzustellen, dass defekte Geräte umgehend repariert werden. Dies ist meiner Meinung nach entscheidend, um die Zufriedenheit der Mitglieder zu gewährleisten und den guten Ruf Ihres Fitnessstudios aufrechtzuerhalten.

Ich hoffe auf eine schnelle und effektive Lösung dieses Problems und danke Ihnen im Voraus für Ihre Aufmerksamkeit. Ich möchte weiterhin Ihr Fitnessstudio nutzen, aber es ist wichtig, dass die Qualität und der Zustand der Geräte sich verbessern.

Context: I've been using pure gym for over 4 years now, I've been to roughly 25 locations across the country, and this one is in my top 3 for worst pure gyms.

Pros:
-Free Parking

-Still cheap considering the current market.
-Freindly Staff
-Free, decent wifi (They Use O2 wifi which is much faster and less restrictive than the Puregym wifi used at other gyms)

Cons:
-Awful and inconistent gym layout (will talk more about this later)
-Lacking in some equipment, and excessive amounts of others
-Not 24 hours (I get its located near residential but the place is pretty much soundproof and pubs are open less than a mile away till much later)
-Awful Music (generic modern pop dribble)
-Only 2 doors to get out and one is usually broke (Happend a good 5 times this year that I can count).

The layout is really what ruins this gym.  I dont understand the thought process of the person who designed this but its utterly idiotic.

So upstairs you have a room full of treadmills, a room full of crosstrainers, a cycle class room full of bikes, a row of rowing machines, and then a little room with some chest, shoulder, bicep, tricep and hip machines. You also have the class for lessons and a little area with yoga mats.

Then you go downstairs, you have a room with squat racks, a deadlift platform, Smith machines, a bench press, a leg press , a pull up/ dip station and a seated bicep curl rack?

You then have a room full of about 15 benches and free weights, with a leg press machine, hamstring curl machine and leg extension machine.

Finally you have a little area that has 2 cable machines, an assisted pull up dip machine, 2 lat pull downs and some back row machines. Then for some reason, this room has a calf press machine???

So to do a full lower body workout, you'd have to go to almost every area of the gym? Going up and stairs during a leg day is never ideal.

The same goes for upper too.

I just don't get the choices made. Like one cable machine is on the complete opposite side of the gym, so if your missing the extension requiren you gotta do a whole lap and hope it doesn't get stolen whole ur gone.

Surley it makes more sense to have all the lower body equipment in the same room, and have all 3 cable machines together also.

There are space restctions, but the layout could be heavily improved.

They also need to increase and decrease certain bits of equipment.

Usually when I go, all benches are taken, however not once have i been there and all crosstrainers have been in use, its excessive, especially considering all the bikes and treadmills too.

The gym only has one flat bench, which is Ludacris, and 1 or 2 more cable machines could be added upstairs next to the existing one.

The gym needs a redesign, and more investment in weightlifting equipment, do this and the gym would be massively improved.

The new Pure Gym opening in Falkirk in September 2023, will be £10.99 for the first 10 months and then £20.99 after that. This will also be a larger gym.
£18.99 after the initial 6 months, would be a much more reasonable price for Linlithgow.

- the studio is also the stretching/warm up/down exercise area. When there are classes, which is most of the popular hours, it is hard to find places to stretch etc. I find this very frustrating.
- studio noise is very loud, including instructor microphone which means during classes it’s all the whole gym can hear.
- the ventilation is awful in this gym. As soon as you enter the building you immediately feel the dirty, stale air and it doesn’t feel particularly healthy to breathe it in. This is a big issue that they should be looking to rectify.
- it’s a very hot gym. I like that as it makes you sweat but can be overpowering when not feeling absolutely peak for a workout.
- the weights room is small, cramped and full of too many benches which makes lifting weights when not using a bench or squat rack almost impossible. - Fortunately I don’t need the changing rooms or shower as live nearby but the men’s is really small and not in great shape. Really not that good.
- There’s only one water tap.

I couldn't agree more with the sentiments expressed in the previous review regarding the bike rack at our local gym.

As a regular gym-goer and an advocate for sustainable transportation, I was excited to see that my local gym had a bike rack. However, my recent experience using this bike rack has left me thoroughly frustrated, especially as the rainy season is approaching.

One of the most glaring issues is the complete lack of rain protection for the bike rack. Living in a region with unpredictable weather, it's astonishing that the gym hasn't invested in a simple shelter or covering for the bike rack. As we all know, rainy days can catch us off guard, and returning to a soaked bicycle after a strenuous workout is far from ideal.

Furthermore, during peak gym hours, the bike rack is consistently full. This overcrowding issue has become a recurring problem, making it incredibly inconvenient for cyclists like myself who rely on biking as a means of transportation to and from the gym. It's frustrating to arrive at the gym, only to find that there is no available space to secure my bike safely.

In order to enhance the overall experience for cyclists, the gym should seriously consider expanding its bike rack capacity. This would not only ensure that cyclists have a reliable place to park their bikes but also encourage more people to choose sustainable transportation options.

In conclusion, while I appreciate the gym's efforts to accommodate cyclists, there are significant improvements that need to be made. Providing rain protection for the bike rack and addressing the issue of overcrowding during peak hours would go a long way in making the gym more cyclist-friendly. Until these improvements are made, I would advise fellow cyclists to explore alternative parking options or be prepared for the inconvenience of dealing with a less-than-ideal bike rack situation at this gym.

It raises the question: what’s the real situation?

It’s crucial to highlight that under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, employers are legally obliged to ensure the health, safety, and welfare of their employees and anyone else on their premises. This responsibility encompasses providing an environment with a safe and comfortable temperature. I genuinely hope PureGym Riverside takes urgent action to rectify this situation. If no improvements are made or if there’s no direct communication regarding this issue, I’ll feel compelled to report the conditions to the relevant health and safety authorities for the wellbeing of all members.

On the initial trial day, I experienced cold showers without hot water, which appears to be a recurring problem. The gym is acceptable, though not the best I've encountered.

In addition to the aforementioned, I would like to provide a comprehensive review of Pure Gym.

The gym seems to embrace a strategy akin to the fast fashion model, aiming to attract a broad customer base through affordable services. While this approach might hold appeal, it appears to prioritize Pure Gym's financial interests rather than delivering optimal value to its members. Let's delve into specific aspects of the gym experience.

Starting with the gym's layout, it exudes a youthful and vibrant atmosphere that more closely resembles a youth club than a traditional fitness facility. The well-lit and energetically loud ambiance, occasionally punctuated by announcements akin to those found in a bustling retail environment, contributes to this unique character. However, during my recent visit, the absence of hot water persisted for a notable period of around two weeks. Additionally, the air conditioning failed to provide respite from external temperatures, resulting in a rather uncomfortable workout environment characterized by continuous perspiration. It is noteworthy that these conditions even extended to the availability of hot water for post-workout showers.

Transitioning to equipment, it appears that Pure Gym might be cutting costs in this domain to offer competitive subscription rates. This decision, while making the gym more accessible financially, comes at the expense of equipment quality. Notably, the equipment, predominantly manufactured by Matrix, falls short when compared to the offerings of established industry players like Technogym. The disparity is evident not only in the cost-effective nature of Matrix equipment but also in its design limitations that could potentially lead to injuries. Specific examples include the suboptimal design of the Lat Pulldown's seating arrangement and the somewhat awkward footrest configuration on the Low Row machine. These design flaws may increase the risk of injuries, and the same concern extends to other equipment like benches and cable machines.

Furthermore, the relatively new gym exhibited signs of wear and tear on the accessories of cable machines, indicating a potential compromise in equipment durability.

Taking these factors into consideration, I made the decision not to become a member of the Pure Gym franchise. Instead, I have opted to invest my resources wisely by joining a reputable gym that prioritizes quality and safety, thereby minimizing the potential risk of injuries and preserving overall well-being. 💪

I recently experienced (1 hour ago) a challenging situation at the gym which compelled me to share my feedback. As someone who greatly appreciates utilizing the functional area, particularly for exercises involving kettlebells, box jumps, the assault bike, and the sledge, I encountered an unfortunate incident during my workout.

During my session, a group class was being conducted by a personal trainer, and they had occupied the entire functional area, leaving no space for other individual workouts. Despite my preference for using the functional area and the available equipment, I was requested to leave the area mid-workout to accommodate the ongoing class. To my surprise, I was even advised to take my 24kg kettlebell upstairs, though I initially presumed it to be a jest.

Considering the gym's size and layout, it would be more appropriate for group classes to take place in the designated class area upstairs rather than overtaking the entire functional area. This way, both group class participants and individual gym-goers can enjoy a more harmonious and conducive workout environment.

I understand that group classes are an integral part of a gym's offerings, but it is equally important to ensure that designated areas are respected to cater to everyone's fitness preferences.

To those who particularly enjoy incorporating exercises involving the sledge, box jumps, kettlebells, pull-up bars, and free weight racks into their routine, I would advise avoiding the gym during the hours of 0600-0700 to prevent any potential disruptions.

As a result of this unfortunate experience, I have decided to discontinue my membership with Pure Gym. I rarely write reviews, but the manner in which I was asked to leave the area was undeniably discourteous and unprofessional.

I hope my feedback can contribute to a more considerate and inclusive gym environment for all members.

The gym's policy of encouraging equipment sharing is in place precisely to ensure fairness and efficiency for all members. We should strive for a balance where personal trainers can fulfill their professional duties while still respecting the needs and rights of other gym-goers. I like this gym facility. This is a protest review against Pure Fitness's predatory cancellation process.

They advertise being "commitment-free". That's deceptive advertising and simply a lie.

Pure Fitness is a hands-off, app-based gym. You join through their app. You use their app to display a QR code that unlocks a tube you step into before entering the building. The QR code readers often malfunction.

If you need to cancel your membership, you go on the app, because everything is run through the app. The app literally sends you in circles with "cancellation instructions". There is no in-app cancellation process. You have to give up and call live chat. Wait for an agent to respond.

Live chat will tell you that "you need to call your bank to end your payment agreement". If you do not stop payment within 7 business days of your next billing date, you will still be charged. EDIT: Response from owner says when cancelling within 7 days of next billing, "best advice is to contact your bank". That's not how it was presented on live chat - cancelling through Pure Fitness's website/app was *not an option*.

They essentially want you to do their job managing subscriptions when cancellation can and should be a single button.

NOPE. I will tell everybody not to join. Tired of gyms exploiting people. I'm a business owner, too. Every membership has a churn rate. You can't hold customers hostage.

The clanging of metal is quite common, and the breaking of floorboards and some equipment was an issue.
